t: Ramesses II ruled Egypt for 66 years, the longest recorded reign of any pharaoh, and built from the Delta to Nubia on a scale no earlier king had matched.
He claimed Kadesh as a great victory, but the battle is generally considered a stalemate, and the war with the Hittites ended in Year 21 in a treaty of which both versions survive.
His monuments served as propaganda for his victories and his divinity, and he was one of the few pharaohs worshipped as a god in his own lifetime.
dyk: In September 1976 the mummy of Ramesses II was sent to France for treatment and received at Paris–Le Bourget Airport with full military honours befitting a king. The persistent claim that it was issued with a passport for the journey is incorrect.
ev: Ramesses is born, the grandson of the vizier and officer who became pharaoh as Ramesses I
He succeeds his father Seti I as pharaoh at the age of 25
He fights the Hittite forces of Muwatalli II at Kadesh in Syria, a battle generally considered a stalemate
Returning to Syria, his armies take Moab and recapture Upi, the land around Damascus
He concludes the peace known as the Treaty of Kadesh with the Hittite king Ḫattušili III
With his queen Nefertari he travels into Nubia to inaugurate the temple of Abu Simbel
He dies aged about 90, early in his 67th regnal year, and is succeeded by his son Merneptah

f.born: c. 1303 BCE, into a family from the far north-eastern nome of Egypt; son of Seti I and grandson of Ramesses I, a vizier and military officer who became pharaoh
f.died: 1213 BCE (13 August by the most detailed reckoning; others give July or early August), aged about 90, most likely at Pi-Ramesses; cause unknown, possibly an infection from an abscess in the jaw
f.role: Prince regent under his father Seti I from about the age of fourteen; third pharaoh of the Nineteenth Dynasty of Egypt, 1279–1213 BCE
f.known: The Battle of Kadesh against the Hittites; the Treaty of Kadesh; the temples of Abu Simbel; the Ramesseum at Thebes; the Delta capital Pi-Ramesses; a 66-year reign with thirteen or fourteen Sed festivals; the Greek name Ozymandias
